darren: FYI observed a small but consistent latency bump (5-12%) on short-chat workloads after flipping the kernel policy to prefer FAv3 when available. Not the usual kernel crossover signature — looks tied to allocation/scheduling rather than math accuracy.

sofia: interesting. do we have traces/alloc logs? short-chat = seq 8-64? batch sizes?

darren: yeah seq 8-64, p50/95 both moved. batch=1/2. attaching quick profiler paste:

```
# perf summary (local e2e, RTX A5000)
workload: short-chat (seq=32,batch=1)
old (fa2 preferred): p50=18ms p95=28ms tokens/s=1200
new (fa3 preferred): p50=20ms p95=31ms tokens/s=1080
alloc logs:
- workspace allocs spiking at init step, a few cudaMallocAsync stalls (~0.4ms each)
- fragmentation metric: free-slices decreased by ~18% over repeating requests
```

max: hmm could be workspace-slice coalescing in allocator + FAv3's slightly different workspace footprint. FAv3 kernels sometimes do extra temp buffers for fused mma. If allocator splits vs coalesces differently we could add higher fragmentation.

anya: do we see same in Dedicated infra or only dev GPU?

sam: ran canary on a small Dedicated pool: same direction, smaller magnitude (3-7%). numbers: p50 +1.5ms p95 +2.8ms.

ci-bot: canary deploy 2024-11-02T09:12Z rolled to pool redwood-dedicated-canary-2 (commit a1b2c3)

sofia: ok looks cross-env. hypotheses: (1) FAv3 workspace layout triggers allocator path that returns more small free slices -> higher per-request fragmentation; (2) scheduling/order of kernel launches changed -> worse overlap with async frees; (3) caching heuristics (KV/prefix cache) push slightly different memory pressure.

darren: I attached a tiny instrument patch I used to log free-slice count and latest-ms between alloc/free calls. snippet:

```
// allocator hook
void on_alloc(size_t bytes) {
  log("free_slices=%d free_bytes=%zu last_free_ms=%d", allocator.free_slices(), allocator.free_bytes(), monotonic_ms() - last_free_ms);
}
```

max: nice. can we reproduce deterministically in a unit microbench that toggles kernel selection only? i.e. same model, same inputs, flip policy env var. If we can't reproduce there maybe it's higher-level scheduling.

darren: already did microbench — reproduces. also tried pinning kv-cache off -> regression shrinks ~40%. so cache pressure interacts.

anya: that points to timing window: FAv3 maybe does less internal caching and relies on larger ephemeral kernels, so we're hitting a path that holds slices longer. Could be our continuous-batching interaction too.

sam: also check cudaMallocAsync thresholds. we saw in other perf work that when free-slice sizes fall below device threshold, calls hit slow path and cause micro stalls. FAv3's temp buffers size distribution might be slightly different and tip the distribution.

sofia: proposed immediate mitigations: (A) add allocator coalesce pass between inference calls (cheap, optional flag) (B) tune kernel-preference heuristics: prefer FAv3 only when batch*seq > X or when allocator fragmentation metric < Y (C) force async free ordering to be before kernel launches in the critical path.

max: +1 to B as quick feature flag. we can compute batch*seq cheaply and fall back to FAv2 for small workloads. low-risk.

darren: I'll prototype a config switch: KERNEL_PREF_THRESHOLD_SEQxBATCH=256. Also will add telemetry for allocator.free_slices and async-free latency.

sofia: testing checklist:
- reproduce baseline microbench and record free_slices over 1000 requests
- flip KERNEL_PREF_THRESHOLD to 256 and 512 and measure p50/p95
- run dedicated canary for 24h with telemetry
- check for regressions on long-seq workloads (must remain neutral)

sam: I'll own canary run and analyze aggregate. max can own the microbench change and rollout gate. anya will validate no change on long-seq.

darren: tiny config patch in my branch, pinging @max for review: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/3245 — contains heuristics and allocator telemetry hooks.

max: reviewing now. quick note: add a unit that fuzzes temp-buffer sizes to ensure threshold isn't brittle.

sofia: thanks team. if heuristics help we'll roll as staged RNG: default keep old behavior for existing customers and enable new pref for new model catalog entries. keep me posted. :thumbsup:

darren: thanks — will post results in ~4h once microbench completes.
